title: Full-Stack Developer
tagline: Own a feature end to end, from the database to the pixel.
about: Full-stack developers build both the frontend and the backend of web applications. In startups especially, you'll take a feature from idea to production on your own: schema, API, UI, deploy.
Breadth is the superpower; the trap is being shallow everywhere. This path goes deep on one stack (TypeScript, React, Node, PostgreSQL) while teaching concepts that transfer.
day: Design a schema, write the API and build the UI for a feature
Deploy and monitor the whole app
Pair with designers and product managers
Fix bugs anywhere in the stack

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick JavaScript and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Frontend
phases.goal: Build responsive, interactive UIs in React and TypeScript.

nodes.d: Semantic structure and modern layout with Flexbox and Grid.
links: CSS-Tricks: A complete guide to Flexbox

nodes.d: Events, async code and fetching data.
Typed JavaScript, shared between frontend and backend.
Components, state, effects and hooks.
Ship good-looking UIs quickly and consistently.

project.d: A React + TypeScript app using a public API with search, filters, routing and a responsive design.

phases.title: Backend
phases.goal: APIs, data and auth in Node.js and PostgreSQL.

nodes.d: Serve JSON with Express or Fastify, or route handlers in Next.js.
Model data, query it, migrate it.
Sign-up, login, sessions and OAuth providers, done safely.
The unglamorous features every app needs.
REST conventions, pagination and error formats; when to use tRPC or GraphQL.

phases.title: Ship it
phases.goal: Put a real product online and keep it healthy.

nodes.d: Next.js (or Remix/SvelteKit) unify routing, rendering and data on one codebase.
Unit, integration and end-to-end tests that catch real breakages.
Preview deploys, migrations in CI, environment secrets.
Run your app and database identically locally and in production.
Know when it breaks and how people use it.
OWASP Top 10 for full-stack apps.

project.d: A multi-user SaaS (for example invoicing, booking or a team wiki) with auth, payments in test mode, roles, email, tests, CI/CD and monitoring. Get five real people to use it.

phases.title: Level up
phases.goal: Depth that separates seniors from juniors.

nodes.d: From slow queries to slow renders: measure, then fix the biggest bottleneck.
links: Use The Index, Luke: SQL indexing

nodes.d: Live updates with WebSockets or server-sent events.
Queues, caches, CDNs and read replicas: scaling a product past the first server.
Talk to users, measure outcomes, cut scope. Full-stack engineers are trusted with product decisions.

interview: Build a small full-stack feature in a take-home (often a CRUD app with auth).
Explain how a request flows from browser to database and back.
Schema design for a given product.
React and JavaScript fundamentals; event loop questions.
Light system design: caching, queues, scaling reads.
